clips.title: The story
paras: A Humble Task is an early rite of duty given by Chief Hawkwind in Camp Narache. As the Chieftain attends to pressing tribal concerns on the Red Cloud Mesa, he asks a young adventurer to venture southeast and check on his elderly mother at the local water well. The request emphasizes communal responsibility, elder reverence, and the daily harmony essential to the tauren way of life.

In the shadow of Camp Narache, every member of the tribe is expected to pull their weight and share in the harmony of life. For young tauren coming of age, tribal duty is not measured solely in battle prowess against quilboars or predators; it begins with basic social responsibility. Chief Hawkwind demonstrates this ethos directly: bound to his post by administrative and defensive leadership, he places his trust in novice adventurers to watch over the community's vulnerable elders.

Mulgore's Red Cloud Mesa relies on vital natural water wells scattered beyond the perimeter of the encampment. Early in the morning, Greatmother Hawkwind left the village unattended to retrieve fresh water from the southeastern spring. In a land stalked by territorial wildlife and encroaching Bristleback quilboars, an elder remaining absent for hours raises quiet concern, prompting Hawkwind to send aid to ensure she is unharmed.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: All members of the tribe share in the harmony of life. We live together and work together.
Our commitment to one another carries with it a high degree of responsibility. I ask of you now a humble task.
My mother set out this morning to fetch water from the well to the southeast of Narache. It has been quite some time now. Perhaps you could check on her for me while I attend to tribal matters here?

clips.title: Completion
paras: You traveled all this way just to help an old woman? My my, aren't you a keeper? Here, take one of these training manuals with you, so you may learn how to contribute to the community.
